properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/16/2022
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 976704
Permit API: 059-23556
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/23/2022
Comments: On 11/16/22 a follow-up inspection of the McClure 3 OG Well site was conducted related to violations issued on 10/21/22 (IR:3444721). I was accompanied by Chase Ambrose (PA DEP).Background:On 10/21/22, during a routine inspection, violations were issued for a brine release at the McClure 3 OG Well Site. Elevated conductivity was observed inside the earthen containment berm that surrounds the production tank. The tank was in poor condition corroded with rust and holes. Elevated conductivity was also observed outside of the earthen berm containment.An operator response was received by the Department on 11/7/21 stating that the impacted material was removed and disposed of, the well does not produce fluid, and a new tank had been installed. Findings:-Elevated conductivity was observed in soil outside of the containment berm and in standing water inside of the earthen containment berm for the production tank (Photos #1). -The berm appeared to have recently been reworked. The substrate appeared to be uncompacted and no temporary stabilization was observed (Photos #3-4).-A new tank was present. It did not appear to have been connected to the well (Photos #5-6).-The area immediately outside of the earthen berm appeared to have been recently disturbed. No temporary stabilization was observed (Photo #6).-Some discarded pieces of pipe were observed inside the berm (Photo #7).-No outlet or shut off valve was observed for the berm drain (Photo #9).I called Bryan Goletz of Diversified to inform him of my findings. Mr. Goletz stated that he would address the spill and berm. The observed elevated conductivity indicates that the spill has not been fully remediated. Outstanding violations of 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.54 are being issued.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/19/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/19/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 992330
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. The area of the pad surface had already been scraped by Tobias Machinery during this inspection. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid in the sump was 2.60 mS/cm. Multiple seeps were observed coming from the well pad side slope and the topsoil stockpile which were flowing into the sump. The EC of this fluid was 3.55 mS/cm. The fluid coming from the seeps had a red/orange rust color to it. Mr. Subra said that EQT believes that the color is likely due to iron content in the soil. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Mr. Subra said that Tobias would be cleaning out the culverts later that day.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-07-25 to Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc in Covington Twp, Tioga county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-07-25
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 857007
Permit API: 117-21997
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Covington Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-25
Comments: The DEP conducted a follow-up inspection of Repsol's Twin Ridge (02-185) well site in Covington Twp, Tioga County on. 7/25/2019 at 0920 hours. The weather was 63 degrees with partly cloudy skies. The act 9 sign was observed at the entrance to the site. The E&S Plan and inspection log were available for review in the mailbox. Company personnel last inspected the site on 7/5/2019. Crew was observed onsite setting up the site for the upcoming frac. After discovering the cement material that has been leaching out of the pad surface into the storm water controls, Repsol has been collecting all storm water from the pad surface in the two basins onsite. The basins remain plugged at this time and water is being pumped out. The water is being stored in a frac tank onsite where trucks are able to remove it from site for disposal. Containment structures around the site are were intact and no leaks were seen. Vegetation has grown in around the pad except for areas on the slope where the cement material is leaching out. Upslope from the basin to the west of the pad, I obtained a field measured conductivity of ~4.5 ms/cm from the water entering the basin. Visually, the fluid was resemblant to the fluid observed last visit. Based on the findings today, violations against API # 117-21997 cited on 6/24/2019 remain outstanding at this site from the previous release. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed. No additional violations noted today. I departed the site at 1010 hours.

Comments: On September 18, 2024 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well Site located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3774486 where violations were issued for an 18-20 barrel release of production fluid from a production tank on June 4, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the production tank that was leaking during IR 3774486 has since been removed from the well site. A well tag was fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it, and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed coming from or near the wellhead. The area where the production tank once (where the spill originated), the slope that the spill traveled down, and the area downstream where the spill pooled up at now appears to be backfilled, seeded and mulched pending vegetative growth. In addition, at the edge of the downslope area right before a forested area began, some black fencing was observed.Several soil conductivity readings were taken in the spill areas (0.0418 mS, 0.0362 mS, 0.0054 mS, 0.0137 mS, and 0.0602 mS) and are significantly lower than the soil conductivity readings taken in the same areas at the time of the spill (Soil conductivity readings taken on 6/4/24 documented in IR 3774486: 1.35 mS, 1.454 mS, Over Range, 7.63 mS, 5.51 mS, and 4.90 mS). Upon inspection of the fence, two areas appeared to be compromised. A stake appeared to be snapped and the fence appeared to be pushed down by sediment, at this time, there did not appear to be any evidence of the sediment overtopping the fence and no erosion or sedimentation was observed behind this section of fence. Another section of the fence right behind a small tree appeared to not be trenched and a gap was observed between the bottom of the fence and the ground. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed behind this section of the fence a this time either.The Department is recommending the Operator promptly properly implement and maintain the temporary erosion and sedimentation (E and S) best management practices (BMPs) to prevent any pollution from occurring.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain E and S BMPs. In addition, violations issued during IR 3774486 shall remain outstanding until the Act 2 Report is submitted, received, reviewed and approved by the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

Comments: On September 18, 2024 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well Site located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3774486 where violations were issued for an 18-20 barrel release of production fluid from a production tank on June 4, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the production tank that was leaking during IR 3774486 has since been removed from the well site. A well tag was fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it, and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed coming from or near the wellhead. The area where the production tank once (where the spill originated), the slope that the spill traveled down, and the area downstream where the spill pooled up at now appears to be backfilled, seeded and mulched pending vegetative growth. In addition, at the edge of the downslope area right before a forested area began, some black fencing was observed.Several soil conductivity readings were taken in the spill areas (0.0418 mS, 0.0362 mS, 0.0054 mS, 0.0137 mS, and 0.0602 mS) and are significantly lower than the soil conductivity readings taken in the same areas at the time of the spill (Soil conductivity readings taken on 6/4/24 documented in IR 3774486: 1.35 mS, 1.454 mS, Over Range, 7.63 mS, 5.51 mS, and 4.90 mS). Upon inspection of the fence, two areas appeared to be compromised. A stake appeared to be snapped and the fence appeared to be pushed down by sediment, at this time, there did not appear to be any evidence of the sediment overtopping the fence and no erosion or sedimentation was observed behind this section of fence. Another section of the fence right behind a small tree appeared to not be trenched and a gap was observed between the bottom of the fence and the ground. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed behind this section of the fence a this time either.The Department is recommending the Operator promptly properly implement and maintain the temporary erosion and sedimentation (E and S) best management practices (BMPs) to prevent any pollution from occurring.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain E and S BMPs. In addition, violations issued during IR 3774486 shall remain outstanding until the Act 2 Report is submitted, received, reviewed and approved by the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/20/2025
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8245167
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/20/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Columbia and Springfield Townships, Bradford County on 8/20/2025 at 0830 hours. The weather was 62 degrees F with rain. The inspection was conducted to assess ongoing remedial activities after a well control incident on 7/13/2025 resulted in a produced fluids release.No remediation excavation activities were occurring today due to the rain. Impacted materials stored within secondary containment (photo #2) continue to be loaded into trucks and hauled offsite for disposal. An interceptor trench was installed around the entire secondary containment on the pad surface that collects fluids and diverts them into a pipe (photo #1) that eventually flows into the trench below the pad's fill slope. Fluids were flowing into the lined detention basin from both the eastern and western lined channels today (photos #5 and 6). Fluids flowing in the western channel were field measured at ~6mS/cm and fluids flowing the in the eastern channel were field measured at ~370us/cm. Less than 6 inches of fluids were currently held in the lined detention basin (photo #4).Resource Environmental collected samples from the three shallow, monitoring wells drilled downslope of the well pad on 8/7/2025. Repsol reported that the samples collected on 8/7/2025 from Monitoring Well (MW) MW04A showed that elevated constituents were reported. MW04A can be seen in photo #10 and is located downslope of the preexisting stormwater basin. During remediation of the preexisting stormwater basin, a large rock was removed and a ~4-inch borehole was discovered beneath the basin (photo #9). Repsol reported that the borehole was ~27 feet deep and was not discovered during construction because it is located on the fill side of the basin and was ~3 feet beneath the native soils. It is unclear at this time if the borehole is causing the elevated constituents found in MW04A. Resource Environmental continues weekly sampling from the three shallow, monitoring wells, streams and various seeps on the fill slope. Repsol intends to have confirmatory samples collected from the soils in the remediated stormwater basin, and then backfill, however, a permanent structure will be installed to allow continued access to the discovered borehole. Resource Environmental was screening and purging fluids from the borehole today. Shallow, monitoring well MW01A has not been drilled yet. A rig is tentatively scheduled for drilling of MW01A and the four deep monitoring wells sometime next week. A puddle within the remediated basin (photo #8) returned a field measured reading of ~360us/cm.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1030 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEECH RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/06/2024
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8207183
Permit API: 081-21812
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/06/2024
Comments: On November 6, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection at the Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. Beech Resources reported a spill of approximately 210 barrels of produced fluid on the evening of November 5, 2024. Beech Resources Don Stevenson was onsite. Mr. Stevenson said that a coupler failed on a freshwater pump connected to a Y fitting that blended with production fluid. When the failure happened the production fluid pump overtook the line and released the production fluid onto the well pad surface. The pad is being used as a staging area for the Delta Well Pad stimulation so there was already equipment onsite. Immediately, a vacuum truck began removing the free liquid off the well pad surface. Approximately half of the well pad surface was impacted by produced fluid spill. Beech Resources and their contractors worked through the night of November 5, 2024 to excavate and remove about 90 percent of the impacted surface. During the inspection, Penn E and R arrived onsite to screen the excavation for further impacted areas and collect Act 2 confirmatory samples. DEP broadly screened the excavation area with a soil conductivity meter and the range of conductivity in the excavation was 200 uS/cm to 2,000 uS/cm. Beech Resources plans to move the impacted soil into dumpsters and have it hauled off site. DEP did not observe any indication of the produced fluid leaving the well pad. Due to the production fluid spill onto the well pad surface violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted. Beech Resources plans to remediate the site through the Act 2 process.

Permit API: 117-21545
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/10/2024
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on the well pad after a release was discovered by the Department on the pad surface on 3/20/2024. I met with Repsol representative Harry Lammy at the beginning of this inspection. The plugging rig is still in operation on the well pad. Six wells are staged for production. Multiple GPUs are present on the well pad and appear to be in good condition.A half-round tank is present on secondary containment in the area of the well pad impacted by the release which was discovered by the Department on 3/20/24. Along the south and west edge of this containment, several puddles of fluid were present which had an electrical conductivity between 2.54 mS/cm to 7.39 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming up this fluid. According to Mr. Lammy, excavation of the impacted area of the pad surface has not yet taken place. He said that excavation would take place after the plugging rig has been moved off of the well pad on 4/11/24. In the NOV response provided to the Department via email on 4/11/24 by Andrew Senefelder of Repsol, Mr. Senefelder states that the elevated electrical conductivity fluid discovered on the pad surface by the Department on 3/20/24 was vacuumed up on the same day. The NOV response also states that Repsol intends to remediate the release in accordance with Act 2 remediation standards.Violations remain outstanding against permit 117-21545

Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp

Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with rods and tubing. The pump jack has been removed from the well, the annulus of the well remains connected to a gathering line. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. The well is not equipped with a well tag, nor is there a site ID sign posted at the location.A tank battery containing four steel tanks and two poly tanks inside of an earthen containment is located approximately 200 feet east of this well. There are indications that production fluids (primarily brine) have repeatedly been released onto the gravel inside of this containment. The soil is stained and specific conductance of the soil is elevated at the western edge where fluid from the tanks appears to have been released, and at the eastern edge of the containment where fluids appear to have been released from a pipeline riser/blow off).Vegetation is absent and deer tracks are very dense on the surface outside of the west/northwest extent of the containment, as it appears the released fluids have migrated through the earthen walls at the natural contour onto which the gravel and earthen wells were constructed. Stained soil and elevated specific conductance continue westward into a roadside ditch of Forest Road 219 until the ditch reaches a cross culvert approximately 300 feet away.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29931, 053-29930, 053-29944, 053-29955 and 053-29945 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. These E and S concerns are considered part of E and S violations that are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29816 (Warrant 2980 #45).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Comments: On March 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Yasenosky 2 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 4111999, where violations were issued for failure to comply with a COA of the Department for failing to restore the plugged well site and access road.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the site within 9 months of well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 2/17/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 11/17/2025 and a well site restoration report should have been submitted to the Department by 1/16/2026.IR 4109921 documents the return of a 12/11/2025 Well Site Restoration Extension Request. At the time of this inspection, a Well Site Restoration Report with a landowner waiver of site restoration has yet to be received. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a mailbox on the ground at the access road entrance, however, a post-plugging site restoration plan was not observed within the mailbox. The access road was observed to still be graveled and unrestored with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. Refer to IR 4168113 for violations associated with failure to have a post-plugging site restoration plan on site.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the plugged gas well site to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. CFS appeared to be spread and removed from the perimeter of the plugged well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to comply with the COA for failing to restore the plugged well site and access road is to remain outstanding at this time as the access road is still unrestored.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Chesapeake) Crain well site located in Rome Township, Bradford County on 9/6/2024 at 1130 hours. The weather was 71 degrees F with partly cloudy skies.This inspection was conducted to follow-up on the remedial work conducted by Chesapeake related to a presumed release that was discovered by the DEP on 8/21/2024, summarized in inspection report #3817547. For information regarding Chesapeake's 15-day Notice of Violation (NOV) response and their remedial work conducted on 8/22, 8/27 and 8/28, please see the Spills and Releases; Reporting/Remediating Releases section below.During this inspection, I observed that the produced water tanks have been relocated (photo #2), portions of the impacted pad material has been excavated (photos #3, 4 and 5) and temporarily placed on secondary containment and covered for later disposal (photo #1). Produced water is temporarily plumbed into a temporary storage tank held within secondary containment onsite (photo #11). A low-point in the excavation area (shown in photo #6) had a small amount of collected fluid which I field measured for electrical conductivity at ~765us/cm. Two areas of damp soil/pad material within the excavation area (see photos #7-10) were field measured for electrical conductivity at >4.0mS/cm, indicating that some portions of the release may still be present. The DEP recommends conducting additional screening and excavation efforts to further remediate the release area/impacted material.The CSL 402(b) violation cited against API #015-23853 on 8/21/2024 remains outstanding at this time. Additional violations may be cited based on the analytical sample results from sample #0983-461. I departed the site at 1300 hours.

Comments: On March 19, 2026, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, 4157162, 4157480, and 4157532. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports and discusses 8 observed culverts along the access road as well as any observed erosion and sedimentation issues along the access road. This Inspection Report is Inspection 1 of 2 and assesses Culverts 1-5. All associated violations discussed in both inspection reports are being issued/continued in just this inspection.A COA with the DEP was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, a rig was on site and plugging operations have commenced.During IRs 4157087/4157136/4157162, the DEP recommended the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan and redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.During IRs 4157480/4157532, the DEP recommended the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan. The DEP recommended the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5. The DEP recommended the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.At the time of this inspection, the E and S plan was present in the on-site mailbox at the beginning of the access road. The DEP did not observed any redlining on site plans to depict and appropriately match on-site field changes (Photo 2). properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 10/13/2022 to EQT CHAP LLC in Sewickley Twp, Westmoreland county. 78A12_ - COMPLIANCE WITH PERMITS - Failure to keep a copy of the permit at the well site during drilling or altering a well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT CHAP LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 10/13/2022
Violation Code: 78A12_ - COMPLIANCE WITH PERMITS - Failure to keep a copy of the permit at the well site during drilling or altering a well.
Violation ID: 972771
Permit API: 129-29003
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2022
Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). The ER and PPC plans were not available immediately upon arrival (see photo 3). A site safety and environmental plan was found in the office onsite. A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.
